summary: The study investigates the oxidation mechanism of silicon in the presence of a thin HfO2 layer using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The oxidation process is found to occur through two stages: an initial fast oxidation driven by moisture chemisorbed in the HfO2 layer, and a slower oxidation process involving molecular oxygen diffusion. The study highlights the role of moisture in promoting oxidation and the effectiveness of HfO2 as a diffusion barrier for molecular oxygen.
evidence: The text states: 'A set of HfO2 films were deposited... by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using either a F-120 reactor (ASM-Microchemistry) or a Pulsar system (ASM). The temperature of the substrate during the growth was 300 °C, whereas the solid precursor (HfCl4 as the source of Hf) was kept at 160 °C.'
